title: Plan deserialization strictness
description: Every deserializable struct that parses an operator's plan refuses a field the model does not define. The paths named here are the operator-authored surface: src/plan.rs carries the flow, its steps and their locators and expectations, and src/sandbox.rs carries the sandbox block. Two modules deserialize outside that surface and are outside the bound rather than exempt by name, for two different reasons. src/inference.rs reads provider responses, where leniency is correct because a vendor adding a field must not break Tinman. src/skill.rs reads the skill Tinman itself ships, compiled in from assets with include_str!, whose front matter carries two required fields and so already fails loudly when one is missing or misspelled; whether an unknown key there should also be refused is a live question rather than a settled exclusion. Discharged by the deserialization-strictness checker in verification support, which reads the derive attributes on each deserializable type under the named paths. Attested by the @contract scenario in features/harness-plan.feature.
rationale: A plan whose step carried a field the model does not define parsed, ran, asserted nothing and exited zero. Tinman exists so that a claim about a program is checked rather than believed, and an assertion that disappears while the suite reports success is that promise inverted, landing on the operator's own test suite rather than on this one. Twenty-one deserializable types sit under these paths and one denied unknown fields. Bounding the modules rather than listing the types is what covers the step or locator a later feature adds, since a type added to a plan is exactly where the next silent drop would hide. An exemption belongs in exemptTypes with a reason, so leniency is always a decision somebody made rather than an attribute nobody wrote.
